definition: Temperance means moderation in action or thought.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word temperance. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know temperance should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Their debate coach preached temperance with evidence: two strong studies, she said, beat ten shaky ones read aloud in a hurry.

Restraint is the milder, moment-sized act beside temperance—declining the second helping tonight says nothing about tomorrow, while temperance is the standing habit of stopping at enough, night after night.
Abstinence goes further than temperance or restraint—the abstinent give a thing up entirely, while the temperate keep it, measured to enough.

Moderation is the everyday word for keeping to sensible amounts—of food, spending, screen time. Temperance is moderation promoted to a principle: a settled, deliberate policy of stopping at enough, kept up over years. You can eat in moderation this week; temperance is the standing rule behind every week.

Self-restraint is the act of holding yourself back, moment by moment—swallowing the retort, skipping the splurge, each one a separate effort of will. Temperance is what those moments become once they harden into settled habit: the principle rather than the push. Self-restraint is exercised; temperance is lived.

At eleven, Mirela could have practiced violin eight hours a day, and wanted to.
Her teacher forbade it, preaching temperance in a field famous for burnout: ninety focused minutes, then the instrument goes back in its case.
The rule never bends -- not before competitions, not after a bad lesson, not even when Mirela begs.
It felt like punishment at first, she admits, and then it felt like the reason she still loved the instrument at seventeen.
Her conservatory classmates, many nursing overuse injuries and frayed nerves, have started asking for the schedule.
